chunks: He said to me: 'Write!' So he dictated to me: 'From our doctrine it is that Allah argues against the servants with what He granted them and made known to them. Then He sent a Messenger to them and revealed the Book to them, and commanded in it and forbade. He commanded in it salat and fasting. So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family) slept through the salat, and He said: "I cause you to sleep and I wake you up; so when you rise, perform the salat" — so that they may know, when that happens to them, how they should act. It is not as some say: "When one sleeps through it, he is destroyed." And likewise fasting: "I cause you to be sick and I cause you to recover; so when I heal you, make it up."'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And likewise when you look at all things, you will not find anyone in hardship, and you will not find anyone except that Allah has the proof (hujja) over him and Allah has the will (mashi'a) regarding him. And I do not say that they may do whatever they wish.'

Then he said: 'Allah guides and leads astray, and He said: "And they were not commanded except with less than what they are capable of." And everything the people are commanded with, they have the capacity for it; and everything they do not have the capacity for, it is lifted from them. But the people — there is no good in them.'

Then he (peace be upon him) recited: 'There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find what they should spend, so long as they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger — there is no way against the doers of good; and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful. [9:91] Nor upon those who, when they came to you that you might carry them [9:92].' He said: 'So it was lifted from them because they do not find (the means).'

key_terms.أَمْلَى: Dictated (to a scribe) — indicating formal transmission of authoritative doctrine
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The proof, the divine argument — a key theological term in Shia theology referring to God's establishing of His case against creation
key_terms.الْمَشِيئَةُ: The divine will, volition — God's sovereign desire regarding His creation
key_terms.سَعَتِهِمْ: Their capacity, capability, scope of ability — the measure of what one can bear
key_terms.مَوْضُوعٌ: Lifted, removed, dispensed — obligations waived due to inability
key_terms.يَحْتَجُّ: To argue, establish proof, present divine evidence against

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia doctrine on divine proof and human responsibility according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) dictates a formal doctrinal position to Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, stating that God establishes proof against His servants only through what He has made them capable of — establishing divine justice through the principle of capacity-commensurate obligation. The Imam demonstrates this through examples of the Prophet's missed prayer (slept through) and illness (preventing fasting), both divinely caused and forgiven, showing that God's proof is grounded in human ability, not arbitrary demand. The hadith concludes with Imam al-Sadiq reciting Quran 9:91-92 to show this principle is embedded in scripture.
